questions.stem: Use each of the six distinct digits 0,1,2,3,4,8 exactly once to make the smallest positive six-digit integer divisible by 9, 11 and 4. A six-digit number may not begin with zero. Establish that your result is minimal without simply citing a computer search.
conditions: All three divisibility requirements must hold simultaneously.

answer.summary: The least six-digit arrangement divisible by4,9,11 is120384.
reasoning: Any arrangement has digit sum18. Its alternating digit sum is 2S_odd−18, an even integer from −18 to18; divisibility by11 forces it to be0, hence odd-position and even-position sums both9. Leading prefix10 fails because positions3 and5 would need to sum8 from {2,3,4,8}, impossible. Prefix12 with digit0 in position3 forces digit8 in position5, and remaining 3 and4 must occupy positions4 and6; ending84 works but 83 does not. Thus 120384 is minimal.
120384 has each digit once and is divisible by4,9,11.
The only smaller prefix10 family fails; among prefix12 completions120384 is the least.
